shop-restore.change: Restore one repair shop without rolling back another shop's accepted work.

restore_scope.question: What does one shop's recoverable state include?
restore_scope.rejecting_observation: The restored request points to missing or wrong-version data.

records.question: Can selected records be reconstructed without replacing the shared table?
records.rejecting_observation: A current record from the other shop disappears or an older revision wins.

photos.question: Do object versions and grants match the restored records?
photos.rejecting_observation: The selected owner cannot open a referenced photo or a neighbor can.

workflow.question: Which assignments and pending jobs have already escaped the database?
workflow.rejecting_observation: A technician is assigned twice after replay.

other_shop.question: What proves unaffected shops retained their current work?
other_shop.rejecting_observation: Shop B's post-backup request is missing after Shop A's restore.

customer_route.question: How does only this shop's customer request reach the selected restored state?
customer_route.rejecting_observation: Shop A still reaches the damaged version or Shop B is routed to the restore candidate.

write_fence.question: Who may write during selection and reconciliation?
write_fence.rejecting_observation: A concurrent write is silently overwritten.

access.question: Who may inspect temporary restore copies?
access.rejecting_observation: A restore operator or application role can read an unrelated shop.

outside_effect.question: How will a scheduler's accepted but unanswered action be reconciled?
outside_effect.rejecting_observation: A retry creates a second technician assignment.

cost.question: What copies, overlap time and verification work enter the full cost?
cost.rejecting_observation: The estimate omits retained restore storage or the temporary environment.

runbook.question: Who approves the return and which customer result ends the drill?
runbook.rejecting_observation: A healthy database is reported while a confirmed request remains unavailable.

school-two-reviewers.change: A document now needs two distinct human approvals after a clean scan.

approval_rule.question: What counts as two distinct current approvers for the exact version?
approval_rule.rejecting_observation: One person approves twice or an approval for older bytes releases new bytes.

review_state.question: How are pending, rejected and revoked decisions represented?
review_state.rejecting_observation: A second approval arrives after rejection and publishes the file.

identity.question: Who assigns each reviewer and what separation is required?
identity.rejecting_observation: An unassigned reviewer or uploader supplies a counted approval.

file_release.question: Which application, object and old-link paths can return the bytes?
file_release.rejecting_observation: An earlier direct link opens the document before both approvals.

audit.question: Can the operator explain who approved which version and when?
audit.rejecting_observation: The release has no attributable two-person decision trail.

retry.question: Can duplicate events or lost replies count an approval twice?
retry.rejecting_observation: One approval event replay satisfies the quorum.

direct_link.question: How are existing URLs, caches and already downloaded copies handled?
direct_link.rejecting_observation: The normal route denies while a previously issued URL still serves bytes.

cost.question: What storage, scanning, review and retained-copy work changes?
cost.rejecting_observation: The estimate prices only the upload request.

transit-alert.change: A bus operator must alert opted-in riders affected by a route closure within five minutes, without issuing a stale all-clear.

closure_fact.question: Who confirms the closure, route, start time and five-minute clock?
closure_fact.rejecting_observation: The clock starts from a later batch run or the alert names the wrong route.

operator_authority.question: Which operator may declare or clear this exact disruption?
operator_authority.rejecting_observation: An unrelated depot can send a route-wide all-clear.

affected_routes.question: Which stops and journeys are actually affected at this time?
affected_routes.rejecting_observation: A neighboring route is alerted while a diverted stop is missed.

consent.question: Which riders opted into each channel, and what may be retained?
consent.rejecting_observation: A rider who opted out receives a message or a private contact list leaks to another route team.

status_version.question: What is the authoritative current closure version and its effective time?
status_version.rejecting_observation: An older all-clear replaces a newer closure.

stale_update.question: How are late or duplicate status events refused or reconciled?
stale_update.rejecting_observation: A delayed clear event is announced after the route closes again.

fanout.question: How are affected riders selected and work divided without losing a recipient?
fanout.rejecting_observation: A retry sends two contradictory messages or a large fanout misses the five-minute deadline.

channels.question: What is the app, email, text and public-stop fallback when a channel fails?
channels.rejecting_observation: The app shows the alert while riders without the app receive no usable notice.

retry.question: What happens after an ambiguous send result and which attempt identity is reused?
retry.rejecting_observation: A timeout is treated as certain failure and a new attempt sends a duplicate or late message.

delivery_evidence.question: Which receipt means accepted by a channel, and what proves a rider saw the current notice?
delivery_evidence.rejecting_observation: A provider acceptance receipt is reported as five-minute rider reach.

rider_result.question: How will the operator observe timely, accessible information for affected journeys?
rider_result.rejecting_observation: Aggregate send success is green while one diverted stop or accessibility path is still wrong.

cost.question: What peak messages, retries, channel rates, logs and retained contact data enter the estimate?
cost.rejecting_observation: The price uses the normal daily average instead of closure-time fanout and retries.

tenant-burst.change: One SaaS tenant sends 100 times its usual work while others retain their deadlines.

arrival_pattern.question: What is the new peak rate and accepted-work deadline per tenant?
arrival_pattern.rejecting_observation: An average hides a burst that exceeds the deadline.

admission.question: Which tenant may submit work and what is returned when capacity is unavailable?
admission.rejecting_observation: The service acknowledges work it cannot recover or finish on time.

workers.question: Can one tenant occupy every worker or retry slot?
workers.rejecting_observation: Another tenant waits past its deadline despite spare entitlement.

database.question: Is the shared data path the bottleneck after worker scheduling changes?
database.rejecting_observation: Fair worker starts still wait on saturated shared connections.

change_rollout.question: How will a new fairness rule enter service without stranding accepted jobs?
change_rollout.rejecting_observation: Old workers stop while their acknowledged tenant jobs have no recoverable owner.

queue.question: Who sets trusted tenant identity, ordering, visibility and retry limits?
queue.rejecting_observation: A sender chooses a neighbor's group or a poison message blocks progress.

observability.question: Can accepted-to-complete time and failure be seen per tenant?
observability.rejecting_observation: An aggregate green metric hides one tenant's missed deadline.

cost.question: What new request, queue, worker, database and log usage must be priced?
cost.rejecting_observation: The estimate assumes the old average after the burst change.
